data.name: Atabul
data.gender_notes: Atabul is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Atabula is an alternate name for the god Agni, who is the deity of fire and is regarded as the god of agriculture, sacrifices, and the purifier. He is also believed to be the conduit between the gods and humanity. The name Atabul carries the meaning “God of Fire” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Atabul usually hope their child will grow to embody god of fire and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Atabul belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Fire.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Atabul total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Atabula carries a deep cultural significance in Hinduism as it is an alternate name for the god Agni, who holds a significant place in the Hindu pantheon. Agni is believed to be present in all sacrifices, rituals, and offerings made by humans. He is also a key deity during various Hindu festivals, such as Diwali, where his presence is invoked by lighting oil lamps.
data.spiritual_significance: Atabula, or Agni, represents the purifying power of fire in Hinduism. Fire is considered sacred, and it is believed that Agni purifies the offerings made to the gods and helps them reach the divine realm. Additionally, the act of offering food and other materials into the fire is thought to symbolize the offering of one's thoughts, feelings, and intentions to the divine. Through this sacred act of offering, individuals connect with the divine and seek spiritual fulfillment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Atabul: The radiant one with an axe, symbolizing the destruction of inner impurities and adversities, leading to spiritual growth and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Atabula, a legendary king of Haihayas mentioned in Skanda Purana, was a great warrior and devotee of Lord Vishnu. He ruled over the kingdom of Vidarbha around 200 BC.

Atavi, also known as Atabhaga or Atabhil, was a famous king of the Mauryan Empire in ancient India during the 3rd century BC. According to some legends, he was a great warrior and a devotee of Lord Shiva. He fought against invading armies of the Shaka king Rudradaman I and was victorious.
